outcome: major depressive disorder (MDD) in early adulthood (ages 20-25 years)
cohort: The study included 534 adolescent oral contraceptive users and 191 nonusers, who were women aged 13-25 years, drawn from the TRacking Adolescents' Individual Lives Survey.
finding: Adolescent oral contraceptive use was associated with a small but robust increased risk for experiencing an episode of major depressive disorder in early adulthood, particularly among women with no history of MDD in adolescence.
followup_time: The follow-up period spanned from adolescent OC use (ages 16-19) to assessment of MDD in early adulthood (ages 20-25), indicating a follow-up of up to 9 years (from age 16 to 25).
